On July 27, 2026, on the third phone call made by the inspector at 3:22 pm, the registrant answered and said that he had
moved to a different city in the state about a month ago. He also stated that he wanted to cancel his registration since he
is no longer transporting animals. He had not notified Animal Care of his change of address and/or intentions, so he was
given the e-mail address to submit the necessary changes in writing. Transporter registrations are only valid for
addresses for which they are issued.
A registrant shall notify the Deputy Administrator by certified mail of any change in the name, address, or ownership, or
other change in operations affecting its status as an exhibitor, carrier, or intermediate handler, within 10 days after making
such change.
Correct by July 31, 2026.

citations.narrative:
A responsible adult was not available to accompany APHIS Officials during the inspection process at 12:42 pm on
7/27/2026. The inspector attempted to contact the licensee/registrant by ringing the doorbell, calling twice and leaving
voice messages each time, and by sending an e-mail. The inspector waited for over 30 minutes and left an Attempted
Inspection Notice on the front wall of the porch to the left of the front door before driving away. Failure to provide access
to the facility, animals, and records for inspection is a violation of the AWA and regulations. Continued failure to provide
access is serious and may result in enforcement action.
End Section
